analyticalQuestion: Can the normalized transport operator be evaluated by an exact all-order maximum over the two admissible input-slope endpoints, and does that remove the R0.39 transport bottleneck?
supportedClaim: For the degree-80 exact center and isotropic weighted Wiener norm, convexity reduces every admissible input slope to x=-1 or x=2, while the degree factor is monotone and reduces every input degree to j=1. The exact polynomial transport norm is therefore max(P_-,P_+). At r=32/125 the full endpoint bounds, including the unknown strict-tail correction, are 0.85855628291965332579 and 0.86219921104223892656. Together with the R0.39 all-order active-tail bound 0.99440931119167253866, this certifies the reduced active and normalized transport fields on the common isotropic polydisc of radius 32/125. At 257/1000 the polynomial transport remains below one but the present active-tail sufficient bound is 1.0002561524370209106.

chartContract.family: logarithmic normalized radius ladder, exact endpoint-column curves, and threshold lollipops
variants: five-stage common and fixed-charge radius ladder normalized to R0.31
both exact endpoint columns for every input degree 1 through 81
six named target, previous-bound, and adjacent-control proof gates
chartContract.takeaway: The exact two-endpoint theorem raises the common certified radius from 397/2000 to 32/125 and makes transport comfortably subcritical; at the nearby 257/1000 control, only the inherited active-tail sufficient bound fails.
chartContract.dataSufficiency: Ten exact radius rows, 162 exact endpoint columns, six exact proof gates, and five finite exact regression rows. Every input slope and every input degree is covered analytically; the finite columns are implementation regressions rather than the theorem's scope.
chartContract.palettePolicy: hard two-root cap: blue and gold plus neutral ink and gray
chartContract.nonColorEncoding: R0.31 through R0.40 use circle, square, diamond, plus, and cross markers; the two endpoints use circle-solid and square-dashed encodings; proof gates use distinct markers, open versus filled faces, and a dashed threshold.
chartContract.finalSurface: single double-column journal figure at 178 by 110 millimetres, with PDF, SVG, and 600 dpi PNG exports

simulation.configuration: active support cone q>=-1; isotropic one-total-degree weighted Wiener norm; exact degree-80 center; target r=32/125; strict active correction tail above degree 80; exact slope endpoints x=-1 and x=2; all input degrees reduced to j=1 by monotonicity; adjacent active-tail control radius 257/1000
simulation.precision: gmpy2.mpq exact rationals backed by GMP 6.3.0; decimal fields are display-only
simulation.solver: deterministic formal-series recurrence, complete exact residual evaluation, exact closed transport coefficient, convex endpoint reduction, monotone input-degree reduction, rational contraction inequalities, and finite exact coefficient/column regressions

tolerances.figure: no fitted parameter; every plotted value is extracted and independently checked against the pinned exact certificates

qa.notes: The PDF page is 178 by 110 mm to rounding and the 600 dpi PNG is 4204 by 2598 pixels. Marker shape, open versus filled faces, solid versus dashed lines, and the dashed threshold preserve distinctions without color.
